statement: The British Museum catalog identifies a silver coin issued by Aksumite king Endubis (museum no. 1989,0518.6), dated approximately 270–300 CE, with a disc-and-crescent motif on both sides; the object is evidence of an early royal symbol, without by itself identifying the precise divine cult behind it.

sources.citation: British Museum Collections Online, Endubis coin, 1989,0518.6, https://www.britishmuseum.org/collection/object/C_1989-0518-6
sources.author: British Museum
sources.access_note: Museum search result displayed accession number, ruler, c.270–300 date, mint, silver medium and disk/crescent description. Direct browser page returned HTTP 403; image, inscription, and numismatic edition not independently viewed.

does_not_demonstrate: A coin motif alone does not identify Mahrem, Astar or Beher-Meder by name.
This is not a first-ever date for Aksumite non-Christian worship.
The disc and crescent should not be assumed to represent an unchanged religious system before or after Endubis.
adversarial_counter: Interpreting disc-and-crescent imagery as evidence of a specific named deity would require inscriptions or contextual comparisons beyond this object description.
notes: Direct artifact page was blocked (403). Catalog text was verified from an indexed museum result only; leave draft pending recheck of the object and numismatic publication.
